summary.intent: Execute all 8 plans in phase 60 (IPNS Verification Cross-Layer Closeout) using wave-based sequential subagents, then run the full ship-phase workflow: verify → secure → validate → simplify → SDK E2E gate → CodeRabbit CLI review → ship.
summary.outcome: Phase 60 executed (7/8 plans code-complete; 60-08 paused at staging-cutover human-action checkpoint). Ship-phase caught a ship-blocking regression via the SDK E2E gate, applied 7 additional security/correctness fixes from adversarial CodeRabbit triage, ran the verify and secure gates (27/27 threats closed), and committed all fixes — but the PR was not yet pushed when the transcript ended.

repo: The gsd-tools commit helper reliably reports `commit_failed` as a false-negative (lint-staged output confuses it) — always verify with `git log --oneline -1` before retrying or assuming failure.
1Password SSH signing agent can wedge after many rapid commits, returning `op-ssh-sign: failed to fill whole buffer`. Recovery requires quitting and reopening the 1Password desktop app.
`gh pr edit` fails on this repo (Projects-classic GraphQL) — patch PR body via `gh api -X PATCH repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/<N> -F body=@file` instead.
commitlint's `subject-no-parens` rule blocks any commit subject containing parentheses; trailing `(D-XX)` tags in executor commits must be stripped before pushing.
`cargo fmt --check` reports drift across the entire workspace due to a local rustfmt version mismatch vs the repo — never run blanket `cargo fmt`; lint-staged does not run rustfmt on `.rs` files.
GSD executors sometimes strand uncommitted Cargo.lock changes after editing Cargo.toml (adding new deps); these create latent `--locked` CI breaks and must be committed separately before wave gates.
ROADMAP checkbox reconciliation may be needed after sequential subagent execution — at least one executor (60-06) wrote a complete SUMMARY and tests but never ticked its own checkbox.
The API log suppresses handled 4xx responses — to diagnose real 400 reasons, temporarily add an axios response interceptor in `packages/api-client/src/instance.ts`, rebuild the chain, then revert.

code.finding: 60-05 removed the equal-sequence enrich that supplied `pubKey` and `signatureV2`/`data` from the DB cached record. For Ed25519 IPNS records, `pubKey` is NOT embedded in the protobuf — it lives in the name. Removing the enrich caused `resolveRecord` to return sig-field-less network results, triggering the strict client's fail-closed throw on every publish→resolve round-trip. Fix: serve the authoritative DB signed record on equal-or-higher sequence.

`parseCachedRecord` must supply `pubKey` from the `FolderIpns.publicKey` DB column (validated at publish to satisfy `deriveIpnsName(publicKey) === ipnsName`). Without this, the strict client has no pubKey to verify the name binding. Codec must also throw on missing pubKey (fail-closed) rather than returning undefined.

`decode_ipns_cbor_validity` used early-return first-wins for the "Validity" key, unlike `decode_ipns_cbor_data` (lines 87-116) which explicitly rejects duplicate "Value"/"Sequence" keys to guard against cross-language parser-differential attacks. Fixed to accumulate and reject duplicates, mirroring the sibling function.

`register_device` used `Err(_) => None` to treat ALL errors as "first device" bootstrap, including `VerifyError::Invalid` (bad signature, expired record). Only `ApiError::IpnsNotFound` (HTTP 404) is the legitimate first-device signal; any other error must propagate fail-closed to prevent a tampered IPNS registry record from triggering auto-authorization.

TS resolve path skipped the entire EOL block when `Validity` was not a `Uint8Array`, silently accepting records with no Validity field. Rust (`ipns.rs:114-117`) fail-closes on absent Validity via `.ok_or_else(...)`. Fixed to mirror Rust: absent Validity now throws, closing the D-07 cross-layer parity gap.

`parse_rfc3339_to_unix_secs` had two leniencies: (1) trailing date/time components (e.g. `2026-01-01-99`) were silently accepted because iterator exhaustion wasn't checked; (2) day validation was only `< 1 || > 31`, so impossible dates like 2026-02-31 passed and rolled forward via Hinnant's algorithm into a *later* expiry — exactly wrong for a fail-closed expiry gate.
The verify cache had no size bound. Under sustained load, a unique `ipnsName:base64(recordBytes)` key per request would grow unbounded. Fixed with a MAX_CACHE_SIZE eviction policy.
Web vault-settings sequence fallback swallowed verification errors (fail-open). Fixed to only bootstrap on true IPNS-not-found; verification failures propagate.

The 60-05 D-06 unit test mocked `parseIpnsRecord` to INCLUDE `pubKey` — masking the regression because real Ed25519 records don't carry it. This false-passing unit test codified the bug. The E2E gate caught what the unit suite missed.

workflow: The SDK E2E gate is the ONLY suite that exercises the real client→API IPNS publish/resolve round-trip; all unit suites mock the boundary and will miss integration regressions like the 60-05 enrich removal. This gate caught 28/89 failures that all 343 unit tests missed.

worktree-isolation subagents cannot expose their branch for orchestrator merge-back in this harness; a security-critical Rust crypto phase should use sequential subagents on the feature branch instead to ensure clean per-plan verification.

Adversarial triage of reviewer findings (spawn N independent skeptics per finding) reliably separates real gaps from false positives — 4/15 CodeRabbit findings were false positives (pre-increment sequence design, already-fail-closed paths).

A unit test that mocks a boundary with idealized data (e.g. always including `pubKey`) can actively hide the regression it was meant to catch. Regression tests should use realistic inputs (Ed25519 records without embedded pubKey) to match production behavior.

When a post-wave build gate flags a compile error, grep for the specific symbol before assuming the executor failed — the error may be a stale mid-edit snapshot; the compiler output at save time is not the final tree state.

friction: 1Password SSH signer wedged mid-session (`op-ssh-sign: failed to fill whole buffer`) after ~28 rapid commits, blocking all subsequent commits until the user restarted the app.
gsd-tools commit helper's false-negative `commit_failed` reports required defensive `git log` verification after every commit to avoid blind retries.
SDK E2E gate revealed a ship-blocking regression (60-05 enrich removal) that 343 unit tests completely missed — the regression would have shipped without the gate.
Stale uncommitted Cargo.lock from 60-01's executor (ciborium/cipherbox-core deps added to api-client) was discovered only during 60-04 and required a manual catch-up commit.
60-01-SUMMARY.md had a stale self-check footer appended after the SUMMARY commit, falsely claiming `verify.rs FOUND` after 60-04 deleted it — required revert.
Workflow tool's `run_in_background` parameter was not accepted, requiring a retry without it.
Web app has no `typecheck` npm script — had to invoke `tsc --noEmit` directly to verify F8.
API log suppresses 4xx, making it impossible to diagnose resolve failures from logs alone without temporarily patching the HTTP client.
